# Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive

## Problem statement

Level authoring in AI_Hell is currently hand-tuned: the five levels in
`src/waves/Formations.ts` are curated by eye, and the only guidance on an
archetype's challenge is a qualitative "Threat level" line in GDD §4.1. There
is no objective, repeatable way to compare two enemies or two waves, so
"deciding which enemies to use in which levels" relies on judgment that cannot
be reviewed, regression-tested, or explained.

## Users

- **Level designer / content author** — needs a numeric, comparable score per
  enemy and per wave while tuning `Formations.ts`, so a wave's challenge can be
  measured rather than guessed.
- **Reviewer / producer** — needs an auditable ordering of the built-in
  campaign to catch accidental difficulty regressions when enemy tuning
  (sliders, JSON configs) changes.
- **Future dynamic-difficulty work** — needs a stable, documented scoring
  primitive it can build on (out of scope here).

Example user stories:

- *As a level designer, I want to see the difficulty score of the enemy I am
  editing in the Enemy Gym, so that I can tell whether my slider changes made it
  harder or easier.*
- *As a reviewer, I want a documented, tested difficulty ordering of the five
  built-in levels, so that a rebalance cannot silently invert the intended
  progression.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deterministic absolute scorer.** A pure TypeScript module computes a
  **normalised 0–100 difficulty index** for (a) a single `EnemyConfig`
  archetype and (b) a wave (`WaveDefinition`, i.e. one or more groups). It is
  **absolute**: derived only from enemy properties, with no dependency on
  player HP, lives, weapons or power-ups. Same input ⇒ same output; no Phaser
  or browser globals required (runs under Vitest/happy-dom).
- **AC2 — Named, documented factors with a per-factor breakdown.** The score is
  composed from the axes named in the work item plus the data model: enemy
  `count`, `driftSpeed` (movement speed), `shotPattern` (attack pattern /
  accuracy), `fireInterval` (attack speed, inverted), `shotProbability`,
  `bulletSpeed`, `burstCount`, `formationKind`, and Asteroid splitting
  (one large = 7 destroyed enemies across the split chain). Each factor is
  normalised over a documented range; firing factors contribute zero when
  `shotPattern === 'none'`. The module exposes the per-factor contributions
  (not just the total) so a score can be explained. All weights and ranges are
  named constants in one place.
- **AC3 — Monotonicity and independence (unit-tested).** Unit tests assert,
  within the relevant `shotPattern`: increasing `count`, `driftSpeed`,
  `shotProbability`, `bulletSpeed` or `burstCount` never decreases the score;
  decreasing `fireInterval` (faster fire) never decreases the score; a
  `shotPattern === 'none'` archetype's score is independent of all firing
  fields; and wave score increases with group count and mix.
- **AC4 — Campaign calibration regression test.** The computed difficulty of
  the five built-in `LEVELS` is **non-decreasing** in campaign order
  (Entry ≤ Descent ≤ The Core ≤ Firestorm ≤ Predictable Death). This is
  enforced by a dedicated test that uses the real `LEVELS` data, so future
  tuning that inverts the intended curve fails CI.
- **AC5 — Usable by designers in the Enemy Gym.** The `GymEnemies` editor
  panel displays the live archetype difficulty score (0–100) for the currently
  edited `EnemyConfig`, updating whenever a slider/select/colour control
  changes it. The readout has a stable DOM id (matching the existing panel
  selector convention) and is covered by a scene-level test that asserts it
  exists and changes after a field edit. Wave-level scores remain available
  from the library.
- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The scoring model, factor ranges, weights
  and the recomputed campaign table (all five levels with their scores) are
  documented in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, with the GDD §3.2
  progression cross-referenced. All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
  or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Absolute, not player-relative** (Producer decision, round 1 Q3 = a). No
  player HP/lives/loadout inputs.
- **Enemy- and wave-level composition** (Q2 = c): per-enemy contributions are
  combined into a wave score; a score exists at both granularities.
- **Design-time only** (Q4 = a): the score informs manual authoring. A runtime
  auto-sequencer that picks enemies to hit a target curve is **out of scope**
  and must be raised as a linked follow-up work item (`discovered-from` this
  item).
- **Deterministic and unit-testable** — must not require a running Phaser game.
- **Additive / non-breaking**: no change to existing enemy behaviour, wave
  spawning, or persisted `EnemyConfig` JSON is required. New fields, if any,
  must remain optional (the `EnemyConfig` index signature already allows
  extra axes).
- **No difficulty modes** (Easy/Normal/Hard) — explicitly out of scope for the
  MVP per GDD §3.1 / AC4.
- **UK English** in all docs and comments.

## Existing state

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — the five levels are hand-authored `LEVELS` data
  with no difficulty annotation; `enemyCountForLevel()` exists but counts only.
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — `EnemyConfig` already exposes every named axis
  (`count`, `driftSpeed`, `shotPattern`, `fireInterval`, `shotProbability`,
  `bulletSpeed`, `burstCount`, `formationKind`) plus the seed archetypes Scout,
  Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Boss Swarm and Asteroid. It has an extensible
  `[extra: string]: unknown` passthrough.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` / `WaveDefinition` — waves are groups of
  `{ enemyKey, formation, count, spacingX/Y, startX/Y }` with a `shootEnabled`
  flag.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — large → two medium → four small; the split chain
  is 7 destroyed enemies; children register dynamically with the wave.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — plain-DOM editor panel with sliders/selects
  and stable DOM ids; the natural place for a live readout.
- GDD §3.1 lists difficulty scaling as out of scope; §3.2 gives the intended
  non-decreasing level progression; §4.1 gives qualitative threat levels.
- No existing runtime "score" concept exists for enemies — `GameState.score`
  is the player's points, unrelated.

## Desired change

Introduce a small, pure "enemy difficulty" library plus its two consumers:

1. **Library** — a new module (e.g. `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`) exporting an
   absolute 0–100 scorer for an archetype and for a wave, with a per-factor
   breakdown. Factor normalisation ranges and weights are exported, named
   constants.
2. **Editor readout** — show the live score in the `GymEnemies` panel so
   designers get immediate feedback while tuning.
3. **Docs** — document the model and a recomputed campaign table, and add the
   regression test that pins the campaign ordering.

## **Key Files:**

- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — New pure scorer: `enemyDifficulty(config)`,
  `waveDifficulty(wave)`, breakdown + factor-weight constants. No Phaser deps.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.test.ts` — New unit tests: monotonicity,
  `shotPattern === 'none'` independence, Asteroid split accounting, wave mix.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — Source of the canonical `LEVELS` used by the
  calibration test (likely unchanged).
- `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts` — New regression test pinning
  the non-decreasing difficulty ordering of the five built-in levels.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Add a live difficulty readout element with a
  stable DOM id, wired to the scorer.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Scene test asserting the readout exists
  and updates when a slider/field changes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Document the model, ranges and
  weights, and the recomputed campaign table.
- `README.md` — Link/expose the difficulty-scoring note alongside the enemy
  config + gym documentation.

## Related work

- **Enemy Design tooling** (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN) — introduced `EnemyConfig`,
  the gym editor panel and persistence. Direct predecessor; the scorer consumes
  its data model.
- **Docs and README for enemy config pipeline** (AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ) and
  **Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide**
  (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6) — documentation homes for the new model.
- **Implement WaveManager — wave and level progression** (AH-0MU72ZK3P006CH9G)
  and **Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to 200**
  (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5) — define `WaveDefinition`/levels and the count ceiling
  the scorer normalises against.
- **Asteroids as an enemy** (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) — the split-chain count the
  scorer must account for.
- **GDD §3.2** (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) — the intended level
  progression the calibration test encodes.

*(An automated related-work report is appended by the find-related skill.)*

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Scope creep into runtime balancing** — the Producer's "possibly (b)" is
  explicitly deferred. Mitigation: record it as a separate `discovered-from`
  follow-up; keep this item design-time only.
- **Weights are subjective** — any 0–100 index embeds opinions. Mitigation: all
  weights/ranges are named, documented constants; the index is relative and
  monotonic rather than an absolute truth; tests pin *ordering* and
  *monotonicity*, not magic numbers.
- **Calibration test could be gamed** — tuning weights to pass AC4 while
  producing a poor general model. Mitigation: also require per-axis
  monotonicity tests (AC3) and a documented breakdown so the ordering is
  explained, not just asserted.
- **Asteroid split accounting is easy to get wrong** — one large yields 7
  destroyed enemies. Mitigation: a dedicated test asserting the split
  contribution.
- **`shootEnabled` vs `shotPattern`** — wave-level `shootEnabled: false` on
  Levels 1–3 means the wave must not be scored as if its enemies fire.
  Mitigation: factor contributions are suppressed for `shotPattern === 'none'`
  and the wave composer must respect `shootEnabled`.
- **Assumption**: a single normalised 0–100 index per enemy and per wave, plus
  a per-factor breakdown (Producer did not object to the stated default). The
  index may be fractional; rounding is a presentation concern only.
- **Assumption**: the scorer lives in `src/core/` next to `enemyConfig.ts` and
  is consumed by the gym scene and docs; exact filename may change.

## Open questions

None — all round-1 and round-2 questions answered.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — What is the primary consumer of the metric?

- **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** "(a) design-time tool and possibly
  (b) runtime auto-sequencer." Final accepted: **design-time tool now;
  runtime auto-sequencer deferred** (see Q4).
- **Research summary:** `src/waves/Formations.ts` is hand-authored with no
  difficulty annotation; GDD §3.1 lists difficulty scaling as out of scope.
  Source: interactive reply.

### Q2 — What is the unit of evaluation?

- **Answer (Producer):** "(c) both" — per-enemy contribution composed into a
  wave/level score with count/formation/mix modifiers.
- **Research summary:** content in the repo exists at two granularities:
  `EnemyConfig` archetypes (`src/core/enemyConfig.ts`) and waves/groups
  (`WaveDefinition` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`). Source: interactive reply.

### Q3 — Is the score absolute or player-relative?

- **Answer (Producer):** "(a) absolute" — enemy properties only, independent of
  player HP/lives/loadout.
- **Research summary:** keeping the score player-independent makes it
  deterministic and unit-testable without a running game. Source: interactive
  reply.

### Q4 — Scope of the runtime auto-sequencer?

- **Answer (Producer):** "(a) design-time scorer only; record runtime
  auto-sequencing as a separate linked follow-up work item."
- **Research summary:** no runtime difficulty/sequencing system exists; adding
  one would substantially expand scope and require a target difficulty-curve
  design. Source: interactive reply.

### Q5 — Where must the score surface?

- **Answer (Producer):** "(c) library + live readout in the Enemy Gym editor
  panel + a recomputed campaign table in the docs."
- **Research summary:** `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` already builds a
  plain-DOM editor panel with stable DOM ids, so a live readout is a small,
  testable addition; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is the
  established documentation home. Source: interactive reply.

### Q6 — Calibration/verification against the existing campaign?

- **Answer (Producer):** "(a) yes" — the scorer's ordering of the five built-in
  `LEVELS` must be non-decreasing, used as a regression test.
- **Research summary:** GDD §3.2 prescribes a clear progression from Entry to
  Predictable Death, so a calibration test is meaningful and catches
  regressions. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X** – Boss appears in both lists on index screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUBZTZ7P00838MH** – Keyboard-driven scene navigation tests (completed)
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH** – Spawn power-ups in all combat gym scenes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absolute, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+310 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+286 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtfp7eic004f1mn, 0mu8bz2zm004j47f, absolute, ac1, ac4 (+253 more)

# Intake brief — Add randomness to explosion

The explosion VFX and SFX are currently very predictable. We need to add randomness to the size and position of the particles in the VFX and to the pitch in the SFX.

## Problem statement

Every explosion currently renders with per-particle size identical to the pattern's fixed base radius, deterministic ring start positions (evenly spaced), and a fixed SFX pitch sweep. Repeated kills therefore look and sound identical, reducing the game's "juice" and making combat feel mechanical.

## Users

- **Player** — perceives richer, less repetitive destruction feedback.
  - *As a player, when I destroy several enemies in quick succession, each explosion looks and sounds slightly different, so combat feels alive rather than looped.*
- **Developer / designer** — tunes the randomisation ranges via constants.
  - *As a developer, I can adjust the jitter magnitudes as named, exported constants and verify behaviour deterministically in unit tests.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — VFX particle size randomness.** Each spawned particle's base radius is multiplied by an independent random factor uniformly in **[0.7, 1.3]** (±30 %). Applies to all patterns (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`) and all entity types. Counts, colours, speeds and lifespans are unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — VFX particle position randomness.** Each particle's emitted start position is jittered by up to **±(0.15 × effective size)** px on both axes relative to its calculated position (this includes the currently evenly-spaced `ring` particles). Applies to all patterns and entity types.
- [ ] **AC3 — SFX pitch randomness.** Explosion destruction sweep endpoints are multiplied by an independent random factor uniformly in **[0.85, 1.15]** (±15 %). Applies to the shared `playDestructionSound()` sweep and the Diver-specific `playDiverDestructionSound()` sweep. The intentionally-unwired Tank variant is not changed. Volume, waveform and duration are unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4 — Determinism / existing RNG.** All new randomness is drawn from the existing seeded PRNG flow (`rng` passed to the pattern emitters; `spawnExplosionParticles` opts.seed). The same seed produces byte-identical particle state. The production seed path (`Date.now()`) is left unchanged — no new seeding mechanism.
- [ ] **AC5 — Test coverage (validation).** New/updated unit tests assert: per-particle radii lie within ±30 % of the pattern base and vary across particles; position offsets lie within the stated bound and vary across particles; SFX sweep frequencies lie within ±15 % and vary across invocations; identical seeds still yield identical output; count/colour/speed geometry tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 visual style and §7.3 SFX catalogue).
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scope is exactly VFX size + VFX position + SFX pitch.** Do not add randomness to particle count, colour jitter ranges, speed spread, angular spread, lifespan, volume, waveform or duration.
- Reuse the existing seeded PRNG (`createRng` in `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — do not introduce `Math.random()` for the new jitter paths.
- All new tuning values must be exported named constants so they remain discoverable/tunable (existing convention).
- Keep the pure helpers pure/testable; do not change the public signature of `spawnExplosionParticles` in a breaking way.
- Production seeding behaviour stays as-is (`Date.now()`); do not add a counter/entropy-based seed.

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` already randomises direction, speed spread, angular spread and colour via a seeded mulberry32 PRNG. Particle **radius** is a single fixed value per pattern group; the `ring` pattern places particles at perfectly even angular spacing with no jitter.
- `src/audio/effects.ts`: `playDestructionSound()` is a fixed `blip(440, 60, 0.28, 'sawtooth', 0.3)`; `playDiverDestructionSound()` uses a fixed deeper sweep; `playTankDestructionSound()` is intentionally unwired dead code.
- GDD §7.2 documents the particle explosion behaviour; §7.3 documents the SFX event catalogue.

## Desired change

- Add an exported size-jitter constant (e.g. `EXPLOSION_SIZE_JITTER = 0.3`) and apply a `[1 - jitter, 1 + jitter]` multiplier to each particle's radius in all three generators (including their `shrinkStep` so particles still shrink to nothing).
- Add an exported position-jitter constant (e.g. `EXPLOSION_POSITION_JITTER = 0.15`) and offset each particle's emitted `x`/`y` by `(rng() - 0.5) * 2 * jitter * size` before velocity is computed.
- Add an exported pitch-jitter constant (e.g. `EXPLOSION_PITCH_JITTER = 0.15`) and apply it to both sweep endpoints in the explosion SFX helpers (applied consistently to start and end so the sweep character is preserved).
- Extend `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` and `src/audio/effects.test.ts` with the bound/variation/determinism assertions from AC5.
- Update GDD §7.2/§7.3 wording to mention the added randomisation and the tunable constants.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — add size + position jitter constants; apply in `generateRadialBurst`, `generateRingBurst`, `generateImplosionBurst`.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` — extend tests for radius bounds/variation, position bounds/variation, seeded determinism.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add pitch-jitter constant/helper; apply in `playDestructionSound` and `playDiverDestructionSound`.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — extend tests for sweep-frequency bounds/variation.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 visual style and §7.3 SFX catalogue wording.

## Related work

- Parent/prior VFX work: **Shared explosion module and constants (AH-0MTVID0YQ001FLEG)**, **Explosion pattern emitters and combinator (AH-0MTVID632005ACBF)**, **Entity-centred explosion colour jitter (AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034)**, **Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V)**.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** randomness should be *layered on top of* existing geometry, not replace it; patterns retain their identity (a ring still reads as a ring).
- **Risk (scope creep):** related "more juice" ideas (screen shake, debris, crackle layers) are out of scope — record as separate linked work items, do not expand this one.
- **Risk:** applying an independent pitch factor to each endpoint could drift the sweep; mitigation — apply a single per-invocation factor to both endpoints.
- **Risk:** radius jitter interacts with `shrinkStep`; mitigation — derive `shrinkStep` from the jittered radius so particles still vanish fully.
- **Risk:** ring position jitter could make the ring look ragged; the ±15 % size bound is chosen to keep the ring legible (validate visually).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Round 1 comment, AH-C0MU0OS0L2002ANZ8): "Scope of randomness — apply to all entity explosion types and all patterns uniformly?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply, 2026-09-22): "1. yes". Source: interactive reply. Research: `EXPLOSION_PATTERNS_BY_TYPE` covers scout/diver/tank/phaser/swarm/boss/player across radial/ring/implosion; all are in scope.
- Q2 (Round 1 comment, AH-C0MU0OS0L2002ANZ8): "Magnitude of randomness — size, position, pitch ranges?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "2. LGTM" (accepting the proposed ±30 % size, ±(0.15 × size) position, ±15 % pitch). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (Round 1 comment, AH-C0MU0OS0L2002ANZ8): "Seeded vs. fresh random — fresh `Math.random()` or the existing seeded PRNG?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "3. Existing RNG, yes. No need to improve seeding though." Source: interactive reply. Research: `spawnExplosionParticles` already seeds `createRng(opts.seed ?? Date.now())` and tests inject `opts.seed`; no seeding change is required.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO** – Pop SFX: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() with unit test (in-progress)
- **AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ** – Swarm has no audio (completed)
- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** – Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_09_22.md` — matched: add, currently, explosion, need, particles (+7 more)
- `README.md` — matched: add, currently, explosion, need, particles (+5 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, explosion, need, particles, pitch (+5 more)

# Intake brief — When player shoots enemy bullet it should explode

## Problem statement

When a player bullet intercepts an enemy bullet, both projectiles are destroyed **silently** — there is no sound effect (SFX) and no visual effect (VFX) at the point of impact. The player gets no feedback that an incoming shot was successfully shot down, so the interception reads as a missed/ignored collision rather than a skill-rewarding action.

## Users

- **Player** — wants clear, satisfying feedback when they shoot down an incoming enemy bullet.
  - *As a player, when my bullet destroys an enemy bullet I hear and see a small impact, so I know my shot connected and the threat is gone.*
- **Developer / designer** — wants one shared implementation used by both the shipped game and the gym scenes.
  - *As a developer, I want the bullet-impact feedback implemented in shared code so the game (`PlayScene`) and the gyms (`GymFormationScene`) cannot drift apart.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Dedicated bullet-destruction SFX.** When a player bullet overlaps an enemy bullet, a **new dedicated** `playBulletDestructionSound()` plays exactly once at the impact point. The shared enemy-destruction `playDestructionSound()` is **not** invoked for this event. Verified by a unit test spying on the audio module.
- [ ] **AC2 — Small impact VFX.** A small, short-lived flash/glow VFX appears at the impact point and is cleaned up when it finishes. The full `spawnExplosionParticles()` particle burst is **not** used for bullet destruction. Verified by a unit test asserting the impact effect is created and torn down.
- [ ] **AC3 — Shared code path (no game/gym divergence).** The bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback is implemented in a single shared helper/module and invoked by **both** `PlayScene._handleCollisions()` (case 2) and `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` (case 2) — the behaviour is identical in the shipped game and the gym. Verified by both call sites referencing the shared helper and by a test in each scene suite.
- [ ] **AC4 — No double feedback on player hit.** When an enemy bullet instead reaches the player, only the existing `_hitPlayer()` feedback fires; the enemy bullet is not also given the bullet-destruction SFX/VFX. Verified by a regression test.
- [ ] **AC5 — Test coverage (validation).** New/updated unit tests assert: the dedicated SFX fires once per interception (and not the generic cue); the impact VFX is created and cleaned up; both scenes route through the shared helper; and no double-play on player hit. Identical inputs remain deterministic.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (VFX) and §7.3 (SFX event catalogue) must record the new bullet-destruction cue.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite (`/skill:test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Dedicated cue.** The new SFX must be a *new* function in `src/audio/effects.ts` (per producer decision), synthesised with the existing `blip()` helper. Short, higher-pitched and low-volume so it reads as a light "tick" and does not mask the heavier destruction cue. Must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests / autoplay-blocked browsers).
- **Small VFX only.** Bullets are ~3 px radius; the effect must be a brief flash/glow, **not** the full particle-burst system (`spawnExplosionParticles()` is explicitly out per producer answer Q2).
- **No feedback on player hit.** Do **not** add a separate explosion when the enemy bullet reaches the player — `_hitPlayer()`'s SFX + VFX already covers that collision (producer answer Q3).
- **Shared implementation.** Implement through a shared helper/module so `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` exercise the same code (producer follow-up #2: "They should share all code"). Do not add two divergent copies.
- **Narrow refactor.** Extract only what is needed for the bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback. Do not consolidate the wider duplicated collision logic here — that is tracked separately in AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO.
- Preserve all existing collision semantics, hit radii (`PLAYER_BULLET_RADIUS`, enemy-bullet radius 5) and consumption behaviour (both bullets are destroyed).

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._handleCollisions()` case 2 (player bullets vs enemy bullets) destroys both bullets with no SFX/VFX (~`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` line 1018).
- `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` case 2 has the identical silent behaviour (~`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` line 1463).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes `playDestructionSound()` (0.28 s sawtooth sweep, volume 0.3) and the reusable `blip()` synthesis helper. There is **no** bullet-destruction sound.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` exposes `spawnExplosionParticles()` for full particle bursts (used for entity/player destruction).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 lists "Player bullet hits enemy — Very short tick, Low volume" but has no bullet-vs-bullet entry; §7.2 covers particle explosions.
- There is no shared combat/collision module: the only two `_handleCollisions` implementations live in the two scenes above.

## Desired change

- Add a dedicated `playBulletDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (short, higher-pitched, low-volume blip).
- Add a small impact-VFX helper (e.g. a brief flash/glow graphic that fades and destroys itself) — a new shared module such as `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`.
- Extract a shared bullet-vs-bullet impact helper (e.g. `resolveBulletVsBulletImpact(scene, x, y)`) that plays the cue and spawns the VFX, and call it from case 2 of **both** `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` when a player bullet consumes an enemy bullet.
- Add/update unit tests for the SFX, the VFX, and both call sites; update the GDD §7.2/§7.3 documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playBulletDestructionSound()`; export any tuning constants.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` (new) — Shared small flash/glow impact VFX helper.
- `src/scenes/combat/` or equivalent (new, if preferred) — Shared bullet-vs-bullet impact resolution helper used by both scenes.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the shared helper in `_handleCollisions()` case 2.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Call the shared helper in `_handleCollisions()` case 2.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Assert the new cue's synthesis/no-op behaviour.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Assert dedicated SFX fired once, VFX spawned, no generic cue, no double-play on player hit.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Assert the same shared behaviour in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §7.2 (VFX) and §7.3 (SFX event catalogue).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "dedicated" means a new exported sound function, not reuse of `playDestructionSound()`.
- **Assumption:** "simpler VFX" means a brief flash/glow — no particle burst — and it need not be extensible to entities.
- **Risk — audio cacophony:** dense bullet patterns can produce many interceptions; the cue must be short and low-volume to avoid stacking (see GDD §6.7 SFX rate-limiting).
- **Risk — shared-helper placement:** both scenes are large; extracting into a clearly named shared module avoids a new divergent copy. Keep the change surgical.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the duplicated `_handleCollisions` logic in the two scenes is a wider problem; it is deliberately excluded and tracked in **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** so this item stays focused.
- **Risk — test coupling:** scene suites boot Phaser; assert via the shared helper and audio-module spies rather than pixel-level VFX inspection.

## Related work

Manual (genuinely relevant):

- **AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH** — Add randomness to explosion (in-progress, high): touches the same `playDestructionSound()`/explosion SFX area; the new bullet cue should not conflict with its randomisation scope.
- **AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M** — Restore gym-game parity (completed, epic): the RCA that established gym/game parity as a recurring concern; this item follows the same "prefer shared code" constraint.
- **AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB** / **AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH** — Core scene collision tests/implementation (completed): cover player-bullet-destroys-enemy-bullet behaviour without feedback.
- **AH-0MU4KJZUE001X6LD** — Extract shared bullet creation utility function (completed): precedent for shared bullet utilities.
- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Consolidate duplicated PlayScene/GymFormationScene collision logic (open, discovered-from this item): the wider duplication this item deliberately does not tackle.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** – Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale and cost a life (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNI1Y001O2OV** – Test: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_09_22.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, explosions, player (+5 more)
- `README.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, player, sfx (+3 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, player, sfx (+3 more)

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (asked 2026-09-16, answered 2026-09-17):

- **Q1 — SFX: reuse `playDestructionSound()` or a distinct cue?**
  Answer: **same** — reuse the existing `playDestructionSound()` (shared with enemy entities). *Superseded (see follow-up Q1).*
- **Q2 — VFX: existing `spawnExplosionParticles()` burst or a simpler effect?**
  Answer (producer): **simpler** — not the full particle burst; a brief flash or glow is preferred, given bullets are ~3 px radius. Research: `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` `spawnExplosionParticles()` is a size-scaled full burst (base count 30, clamped 8–80) — visually too heavy for a 3 px bullet.
- **Q3 — Scope: should the enemy bullet also explode when it hits the player?**
  Answer (producer): **no** — the existing `_hitPlayer()` SFX + VFX for the player is sufficient at the collision point.
- **Q4 — Consistency: dedicated sound or the generic one?**
  Answer: **dedicated** — bullet destruction should have its own dedicated sound cue, not reuse `playDestructionSound()`. *(Conflicted with Q1; see follow-up Q1.)*

Follow-up round (asked 2026-09-22, answered 2026-09-22) — resolves the Q1/Q4 contradiction:

- **Follow-up Q1 — Which SFX answer wins, Q1 ("same") or Q4 ("dedicated")?**
  Answer (producer): **Dedicated.** Create a bullet-specific cue — do not reuse `playDestructionSound()`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Follow-up Q2 — Scope: shipped game only, or should the gym core be mirrored?**
  Answer (producer): "There shouldn't be different core code in the shipped game and the gym scenes. They should share all code." Source: interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each define their own `_handleCollisions` (no shared combat module), so the impact feedback must be delivered through a shared helper used by both; wider consolidation of the duplicated collision logic is a separate follow-up (AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO, discovered-from this item).

Open questions: none — all clarifications answered.

# Leaderboard: Game-Over Score Entry and localStorage Display

## Problem Statement

The game currently has no scoring system, no game-over screen, and no leaderboard. When the player runs out of lives, the game respawns infinitely with no termination. The player has no way to record or view their high scores.

## Users

- **Player**: Completes the game (or dies) and wants to record their score by entering 3-character initials. They want to see their scores ranked against previous attempts on the game-over screen and from the main menu.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I run out of lives, I want to see my final score and be prompted to enter my initials so I can record my achievement.
- As a player, after entering my initials, I want to see the full leaderboard ranked by score so I can see how I compare to my past scores.
- As a player, from the main menu, I want to view the leaderboard to see my best scores.

## Original Acceptance Criteria (superseded 2026-09-22)

1. **Score tracking**: Each enemy type has a defined `scoreValue`. When an enemy is destroyed, its `scoreValue` is added to the player's total score. The score is displayed in the HUD (top-right corner, neon-styled numeric display).

2. **Game-over condition**: When the player's lives reach 0 (starting at 3, max 5 via P8 Extra Life), the game stops respawning and transitions to the game-over screen. There is no continue mechanic. The game-over screen shows the final score, an option to save (if score qualifies), and a restart button.

3. **Initials entry**: On the game-over screen, the player is prompted to enter exactly 3 uppercase letters (A-Z) as initials. Input is validated (only A-Z accepted, exactly 3 characters). [ASSUMPTION: on-screen clickable keyboard styled to match the neon terminal aesthetic.]

4. **localStorage persistence**: Entries are stored in browser localStorage under the key `ai_hell_leaderboard`. The stored data is a JSON array of entry objects (max 10 entries). When a new score qualifies for the leaderboard (i.e., would rank within the top 10), the player can enter initials to save it. If the score does not qualify, the player is informed and may skip the entry.

5. **Leaderboard display**: The game-over screen displays the full leaderboard showing rank, initials, score, and date for each entry, sorted by score (highest first). The leaderboard is also accessible from the main menu.

## Constraints

- Browser `localStorage` only (no backend, per GDD §5.1 — "single-machine" MVP).
- Maximum 10 leaderboard entries.
- Initials must be exactly 3 characters, uppercase letters only.
- Date format: ISO YYYY-MM-DD (per GDD data model example).
- The leaderboard data structure must support future abstraction for online leaderboards (GDD §5.3 migration note).

## Existing State

- **No score tracking exists**: No `scoreValue` on enemies, no score counter, no score display.
- **No game-over condition**: The `GymFormationScene` has infinite respawn — when all enemies are wiped, the formation respawns regardless of player lives.
- **Lives tracking exists**: `EffectsRegistry` tracks lives (starts at 3, caps at 5), displayed via the HUD. But lives are never decremented on player death.
- **No main menu**: The only entry scene is `GymIndex` (dev-mode gym scene launcher). No `MainMenuScene` exists.
- **No leaderboard code**: No localStorage operations for leaderboard, no initials input, no game-over screen.
- **GDD references**: `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts` are predicted but not yet implemented.

## Desired Change

1. **`src/core/Leaderboard.ts`** — Leaderboard persistence module:
   - `getEntries()`: Read and parse entries from localStorage.
   - `addEntry(initials: string, score: number)`: Add a new entry, maintain max 10, sort by score.
   - `getTopN(n: number)`: Return top N entries.
   - `isQualifying(score: number)`: Check if score would make the top 10.
   - Data structure: `{ rank, initials, score, date }` per GDD §5.2.

2. **Score tracking in `GymFormationScene`**:
   - Assign `scoreValue` to each enemy type (Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50 per, Boss: 1000 — [ASSUMPTION values, to be confirmed]).
   - Track player score as a counter in the scene.
   - Add score to total on enemy destroy.
   - Display score in the HUD (top-right).

3. **Game-over screen (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`)**:
   - Displays final score, player initials input, and leaderboard.
   - Neon-styled UI matching the game aesthetic.
   - On-screen 3x3 grid keyboard for initials entry.
   - "Submit" button validates and saves the entry.
   - "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex for now).

4. **Main menu (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`)**:
   - "Play" button to start the game.
   - "Leaderboard" button to view the full leaderboard.
   - "Gym" button to access the gym index.
   - [NOTE: Main menu creation scope — see open questions.]

5. **Lives integration**:
   - Decrement lives on player hit (when invulnerable period ends).
   - When lives reach 0, transition to game-over screen.
   - Stop the respawn loop when game-over is triggered.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope risk — main menu creation**: Creating a full main menu scene is a significant addition. If scope is constrained, the leaderboard may be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead, with the main menu deferred to a separate work item.
- **Scope risk — score tracking from scratch**: No score infrastructure exists. Implementing scoreValue on all enemy types, the score counter, and HUD display adds non-trivial work to GymFormationScene.
- **Assumption — enemy score values**: The GDD defines `scoreValue` on enemies but does not specify numeric values. The values in the draft are estimates and should be tuned.
- **Assumption — keyboard UI**: On-screen clickable keyboard was assumed; a producer decision is needed on input mechanism.
- **Assumption — game-over restart flow**: "Restart" returns to main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu). No "Play Again" shortcut from game-over.
- **Scope guard**: Level progression, boss mechanics, difficulty scaling, online leaderboards, and persistent game state between sessions are out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — New file: leaderboard localStorage persistence
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — New file: game-over screen with initials input and leaderboard display
- `src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts` — New file: main menu with leaderboard access [scope TBD]
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Modify: add score tracking, game-over condition, lives decrement
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Modify: add score display (top-right)
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/*.ts` — Modify: add `scoreValue` to enemy types
- `src/core/Game.ts` — Modify: register new scenes, update boot flow
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Modify: add MainMenu/GameOver to scene list for shipped build

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTZWZ1MQ004L552**: Create a playable game (parent epic, high priority, in `idea` stage) — includes main menu and playable game scope. This work item is a child of this epic.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR**: Leaderboard — discovered-from the playable-game epic; the GDD (§5) is the authoritative spec.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.
- **GDD §6.4**: Technical architecture — predicted `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts`.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes (gym scenes where power-up layer is shared) — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q1**: Main menu scope — Should this work item include creating the Main Menu scene (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`), or should that be a separate work item? The GDD references `src/ui/Menu.ts` ("Main menu, game-over screen") but it has not been implemented. The leaderboard must be "accessible from the main menu" per the work item description. **Assumption**: This work item creates the main menu scene with leaderboard access. If the producer disagrees, the main menu creation should be a separate work item, and the leaderboard should be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead (or from the game-over screen itself).

- **Q2**: Score tracking scope — Should this work item include implementing score tracking from scratch (enemy `scoreValue` assignment, score counter, HUD display, points on destroy), or should score tracking be a prerequisite completed by a separate work item? **Assumption**: Score tracking is included in scope — it is fundamental to the leaderboard feature.

- **Q3**: Initials input mechanism — How should the 3-character initials entry work? Options: (a) on-screen clickable keyboard (A-Z grid, neon-styled), (b) browser-native text input styled with CSS, (c) other mechanism. **Assumption**: On-screen clickable keyboard matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q4**: Enemy `scoreValue` values — What point values should each enemy type carry? Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm (per-unit), Boss? **Assumption**: Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50, Boss: 1000. These can be tuned later via the game-rules config.

- **Q5**: Score format — Should the score display show formatted numbers (e.g., "50,000") or raw (e.g., "50000")? **Assumption**: Raw numeric display (no commas) matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q6**: Game-over flow — After submitting a score (or declining to submit), should the game-over screen offer a "Restart" button that returns to the main menu, or should it auto-restart? **Assumption**: "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu exists). "Play Again" is not available until a score is submitted or declined.

---

## Plan Clarifications (2026-09-22)

### Reconciled current state (verified against source)

The *Existing State* section above was written before the playable game landed.
The following are now **implemented** and are therefore *not* part of the remaining work:

- **Score tracking** — `PlayScene.SCORE_VALUES` awards points on enemy/boss destruction, `GameState.addScore()` accumulates them, and the score is rendered top-right in `PlayScene._buildHudText()` (`Score: N`). GDD §4.5 values are authoritative.
- **Game-over condition** — `PlayScene._loseLife()` calls `_finishRun(false)` when `lives <= 0`, transitioning to `GameOverScene` with the final score. There is no continue mechanic.
- **Main menu** — `MenuScene` exists (Play Game / Settings / Gym Scene Index) and is the boot scene (`gameConfig.ts`).
- **Initials entry** — `GameOverScene` implements the GDD §5.1 in-canvas keyboard model (A–Z, Backspace, exactly 3, Enter auto-submit) via the shared `FocusManager`.
- **Leaderboard stub** — `GameOverScene` contains `readLeaderboard()` / `saveScoreEntry()` persisting `{initials, score}` to `ai_hell_leaderboard`, displaying only the top 3. This is the placeholder this work item replaces.

### Producer decisions (2026-09-22)

- **Q1 — Scope:** confirmed. This work item covers the **remaining gap only** (leaderboard module, qualifying/skip UX, date, full display, menu access, stub retirement). It does not re-implement score tracking, game-over or the main menu.
- **Q2 — Initials input mechanism:** confirmed **keyboard entry only** (GDD §5.1). The earlier on-screen clickable-keyboard assumption is superseded — no on-screen keyboard is required.
- **Q3 — Main-menu access:** option **(a)**. Main-menu leaderboard access is in scope for this work item; AH-0MU9LJ52C00613RX is absorbed/relinked as a child so it is not duplicated.

### Interview record (2026-09-22, plan round 1)

- **Q1**: Scope this item to the *remaining gap*, not re-implementation? **Answer (producer):** yes — remaining gap. Final: yes.
- **Q2**: Confirm keyboard entry (GDD §5.1); no on-screen clickable keyboard? **Answer (producer):** confirmed. Final: keyboard-only.
- **Q3**: Main-menu leaderboard — (a) include here and absorb/relink AH-0MU9LJ52C00613RX, or (b) leave to that item? **Answer (producer):** (a). Final: include here.
- **OPEN QUESTION (resolved):** the automated effort/risk pre-check reported Extra Small / Low with a 0.0h degenerate placeholder; treated as unreliable and overridden in favour of full planning. Recorded in comment AH-C0MU6XUY0S001BIWP.

## Acceptance Criteria (revised, authoritative)

AC1–AC3 are retained as *already satisfied* and are verified by existing tests; they require no new work. AC4–AC6 are the remaining, testable acceptance criteria.

**Already satisfied (no remaining work):** AC1 score tracking (per-enemy `scoreValue`, HUD top-right; verified by `PlayScene`/`GameState`/HUD tests); AC2 game-over condition (lives reach 0 then final score, no continue; verified by `SceneNavigation.test.ts`); AC3 initials entry (3 uppercase A–Z, Enter auto-submit, keyboard-only per producer Q2; verified by `GameOverScene.test.ts`). These are recorded for completeness and are not covered by new child work items.

The remaining acceptance criteria are:

- **AC4 — Leaderboard persistence module** — `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` exports getEntries, addEntry, getTopN and isQualifying, storing `{rank, initials, score, date}` entries (max 10) under `ai_hell_leaderboard`.
- **AC5 — Qualifying and skip UX** — A qualifying score prompts for initials and persists on submit; a non-qualifying score shows an explanatory message and can be skipped with no write.
- **AC6 — Leaderboard display** — The game-over screen displays rank, initials, score and date for all up to 10 entries, highest first, and the main menu control displays the same full leaderboard.

# Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen

## Problem statement

Player and enemy bullets are currently destroyed the moment they cross a small off-screen margin (`radius * 3` for player bullets, a fixed 20 px for enemy bullets), so every shot vanishes at the screen edge. This is inconsistent with the player ship and asteroids, which wrap across all four screen edges, and it prevents bullets from crossing the playfield seam. Bullets should instead wrap around the screen like the ship/asteroids and remain effective only for a bounded range before expiring.

## Users

- **Players** — benefit from shots that travel across the whole playfield and can threaten targets on the far side of the seam, matching the "classic Asteroids" wrap model used everywhere else in the game. A bounded range keeps the screen from filling with permanent bullets and keeps the difficulty fair.
- **AI agents / human developers** — need an unambiguous rule for how long each bullet type lives (and therefore its effective range) so implementations and balance tuning do not diverge.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my bullets to wrap around the screen edges so that a shot can hit an enemy that has just crossed the seam, instead of disappearing.
- As a **player**, I want enemy bullets to wrap too, so the hazard model is consistent and I can't exploit the seam by hiding just off an edge.
- As a **developer**, I want each weapon / enemy bullet type to have its own configurable lifetime, so the Cannon, Spread, Dual, Rapid, and each enemy pattern can be tuned independently without touching shared code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Player bullets wrap:** Player bullets that cross any screen edge reappear at the opposite edge (four-edge wrap matching the player ship and asteroid model) and remain live after wrapping; they are no longer destroyed merely for leaving the screen. Verified by unit tests for each of the four edges plus a corner (both axes) case.
- [ ] **AC2 — Enemy bullets wrap:** All enemy bullets (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Boss Swarm / Central AI patterns) wrap across all four screen edges the same way. Verified by unit tests for each edge on an enemy bullet.
- [ ] **AC3 — Range measured as a per-type lifetime:** Each bullet type has its own configurable **lifetime in seconds**. A bullet wraps for the duration of its lifetime and is destroyed when the lifetime elapses. The effective pixel range is therefore `bulletSpeed × lifetime`. No bullet is culled solely by off-screen position. Player-weapon lifetimes live on `WeaponDefinition` in `src/utils/weapons.ts`; enemy-bullet lifetimes live on `EnemyConfig` in `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`. Verified by tests that (a) a bullet survives one wrap, (b) a bullet is destroyed only once its lifetime exceeds its type's value, and (c) two bullet types with different lifetimes expire at different times.
- [ ] **AC4 — Sane defaults, tunable:** The defaults below are shipped and overridable via the existing weapon / enemy config surfaces (and, for enemies, the existing localStorage config plumbing). Values are proposals to be confirmed at planning:
  - Player weapons (all at `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` = 350 px/s): Cannon 3.0 s (≈1050 px), Spread 2.8 s (≈980 px), Dual 2.8 s (≈980 px), Rapid 1.5 s (≈525 px).
  - Enemy bullets: Scout 3.0 s (200 px/s ≈ 600 px), Diver 3.0 s (220 px/s ≈ 660 px), Tank 4.0 s (150 px/s ≈ 600 px), Phaser 3.5 s (180 px/s ≈ 630 px), Swarm 3.0 s (180 px/s ≈ 540 px), Boss Swarm 4.0 s (160 px/s ≈ 640 px).
  - Verified by unit tests asserting the config exposes a distinct lifetime per weapon and per enemy type and that the scene spawn helpers propagate it.
- [ ] **AC5 — Collision and lifecycle integrity:** Existing bullet lifecycles still hold: player bullets are consumed on hitting an enemy/boss, player and enemy bullets annihilate each other on contact, enemy bullets are cleared by P4 Bomb, and all bullets are cleared on scene restart/pause. A wrapped bullet remains collidable at its new position. Verified by the existing PlayScene collision/pause/mineral suites plus a new test that a wrapped bullet still destroys an enemy.
- [ ] **AC6 — GDD updated:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` documents the new rule — bullets wrap across all four edges and expire after a per-type lifetime (effective range) — in the relevant bullet/auto-fire sections (at least §2.3 auto-fire and §4.4 weapon description, and any enemy bullet-pattern notes). Verified by reviewing the document for internal consistency (no lingering "off-screen cull" wording).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover wrap on all four edges (player and enemy), lifetime expiry, per-type lifetime differences, and post-wrap collision; the existing scene-level suites continue to pass. Verified by running the test suite.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation updated:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Test suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wrap model must reuse the project's existing four-edge wrap semantics (leave left → reappear right, etc.), i.e. the same model as `src/utils/movement.ts` (`step`) and `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` (`updatePosition`) — not a new/alternative wrapping scheme.
- Player bullets remain pure `Graphics` objects (no physics body), consistent with the existing `PlayerBullet`/`ScoutBullet` precedent.
- Range is expressed as a **lifetime in seconds** (operator decision), not a pixel budget; the title's "distance" is realised as `speed × lifetime`.
- No seam-spanning collision semantics are in scope: wrapping is positional only, matching the ship/asteroid model (which also does not detect collisions across the seam).
- This change applies to **both** player and enemy bullets (operator decision).
- Scope is bullet range + wrap only. Rebalancing enemy fire rates, bullet speeds, patterns, or drop rates is out of scope and should be raised as separate work items.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — `advance(dt)` integrates velocity; `advanceAndCull(bullet, dt, width, height)` advances and returns `false` (cull) when the bullet passes `radius * 3` beyond any edge. No lifetime / range field exists.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_advanceBullets(dt)` advances enemy bullets inline and destroys them via `_offScreen` (fixed 20 px margin); player bullets are filtered through `advanceAndCull`. `spawnPlayerBullet` / `spawnEnemyBullet` create bullets with no lifetime; `PlayEnemyBullet` is `{ graphics, vx, vy }`.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WeaponDefinition` (offsets, fireRateMs, bulletColor, bulletShape, bulletSize) for `cannon`/`spread`/`dual`/`rapid`; single `BULLET_SPEED = 350`; `bulletForShot`/`allBulletsForShot`/`createBulletsFromHeading` build shot descriptors.
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — `EnemyConfig` carries `bulletSpeed`, `bulletColor`, `bulletSize`, `shotPattern`, `fireInterval`, `burstCount`, `shotProbability` for scout/diver/tank/phaser/swarm/boss/asteroid; no `bulletLifetime`.
- `src/utils/movement.ts` — `step()` applies the four-edge wrap used by the player; `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — `updatePosition()` wraps asteroids the same way.
- Gym scenes (`src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) also call `advanceAndCull` and must follow the new behaviour.
- The GDD currently documents off-screen cull for player bullets (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 architecture note: "PlayerBullet.ts — Player-fired projectile (Graphics, vx/vy, off-screen cull)") and describes enemy bullet patterns without stating a range/lifetime.

## Desired change

1. Add a per-type **lifetime** to bullets:
   - `PlayerBullet` gains a `lifetime` (seconds) field and an elapsed-time counter; `advanceAndCull` (or a renamed/reworked equivalent) wraps position on all four edges and culls only when lifetime is exhausted, never by off-screen position.
   - `WeaponDefinition` gains a `bulletLifetime` value; `spawnPlayerBullet` receives and stores it (so tests and the scene can set it deterministically).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Interpretation (confirmed):** "distance" is implemented as a per-type **lifetime in seconds** (operator answer Q2b); effective range = `bulletSpeed × lifetime`. If the operator actually wants a hardcoded pixel budget, this must be revisited before implementation.
- **Scope (confirmed):** applies to **both** player and enemy bullets (Q1c).
- **Per-type lifetimes (confirmed as intent):** each weapon and each enemy bullet type has its own lifetime (Q3 "individual"). The specific default values in AC4 are **proposals** and must be confirmed/tuned during planning or playtesting.
- **Difficulty/performance risk:** wrapping bullets stay alive longer, so more bullets may be on screen; the lifetime caps this, but values need playtesting. If performance or difficulty regresses, tune lifetimes (no architectural change).
- **Seam collisions out of scope:** wrapping is positional only, matching the ship/asteroid model; a bullet near the left edge will not collide with a target near the right edge. Documenting this avoids a "why didn't I hit them" bug report being treated as this item's failure.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not rebalance enemy fire rates/speeds, add bullet trails, or add per-level bullet caps here — record as linked work items.
- **Test/API churn:** changing `advanceAndCull`'s semantics touches gym scenes and their tests; keep the signature additive where possible (e.g. pass lifetime) and update all call sites in one change.
- **Assumption:** `GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT` (960 × 540) are the wrap bounds for bullets, matching the ship/asteroids.
